No rent, psf or project is named
Tenant demand and buyer demand are different
An easy rental does not guarantee an easy resale
questions: A one-bedroom can be easy to rent and hard to sell. Which of those two are you about to rely on?
The exit is the moment that matters if you need to sell. What recent sale in your project have you checked?
What are you still waiting to feel sure about, while another buyer looks at the same unit?
takeaways: The headline separates two markets. Tenants and buyers are not the same people. A one-bedroom that rents easily can still sit unsold. No rent, no price per square foot and no project are named, so nobody should buy or sell a unit off this headline alone. An investor who underwrites the rent and ignores the exit is taking the risk the headline is pointing at. Waiting does not thicken a thin resale pool.

Sellers of one-bedrooms should price for the buyer who is hesitating, not for the tenant who is easy to find. The future buyer of a small condo is a smaller group than the tenant pool. An owner who needs to sell may have to accept that the rental story is not the resale story. Holding for a buyer who looks like the tenant is how these units stay on the market.

The direction being claimed is softer buyer interest in one-bedrooms, with renting still easier than selling. That is a product warning inside the condo market, not a call on all private homes. Without a figure, the size of the gap cannot be known. The useful point is the gap itself.
9774.description: One-bedroom condos can be easy to rent and hard to sell. Investors should check resale demand, not only the rent.
9774.keywords: Singapore property, condo, one-bedroom, rent, resale, investors, buyers, sellers

zh.title: 一房式公寓好租难卖，买家兴趣可能在减退
summary: 标题说，新加坡的一房式私人公寓可能好租、难卖，买家的兴趣也许在减退。标题里没有空置率、没有每平方英尺的价钱，也没有项目名称。重点是租客和买家不是同一群人。
租客只要地点适合一个人或一对夫妻，就可以付租金。买下同一套单位的人，必须相信以后还有人接手，而且价钱盖得住贷款。当后面那个买家变少，屋主是在卖出的时候才感觉到，不是在出租的时候。
只查过租金的投资者，还应该看这个项目一房单位的近期成交。以后想换大房子自住的人，要问退出容不容易。一套一个星期就租掉的单位，仍可能挂几个月卖不掉。
facts: 标题：一房式公寓可能好租、难卖
没有租金、每平方英尺价钱或项目名称
租客的需求和买家的需求不是同一件事
好租并不保证好卖
questions: 一房式可以好租、难卖。你准备依靠的是哪一种？
如果你需要卖，出口才是要紧的一刻。你查过项目里哪一宗最近的成交？
另一个买家在看同一个单位的时候，你还在等什么才觉得确定？
takeaways: 标题把两个市场分开。租客和买家不是同一群人。一套好租的一房式，仍可能卖不掉。没有租金、没有每平方英尺价钱、也没有项目名称，所以没有人该只凭这个标题买卖一套单位。投资者如果只算租金、不算退场，接的就是标题指出的风险。再等，也不会把薄的转售买家池变厚。
一房的卖家，该按犹豫的买家来定价，不是按好找的租客。小公寓的未来买家，比租客池小。需要卖的业主，可能得接受租金的故事不是转售的故事。守着一个看起来像租客的买家，就是这些单位留在市场上的原因。
被主张的方向，是一房式的买家兴趣转软，而出租仍比出售容易。这是公寓市场里的一个产品提醒，不是对所有私宅的判断。没有数字，差距有多大无法知道。有用的是这个差距本身。
keypoints: 标题：一房式公寓可能好租、难卖
没有租金、每平方英尺价钱或项目名称
租客的需求和买家的需求不是同一件事
好租并不保证好卖
差距出现在业主想卖的时候，不是出现在租客付租金的时候。
Headline: one-bedroom condos may be easier to rent than to sell
No rent, psf or project is named
Tenant demand and buyer demand are different
An easy rental does not guarantee an easy resale
The gap shows up when the owner wants to sell. It does not show up when a tenant is paying the rent.

summary: EdgeProp reported that HDB resale transactions jumped 19.5% quarter on quarter in the third quarter of 2026, and linked the rise to policy changes. The headline does not say which rule changed, and it does not say prices rose by 19.5%. Transactions and prices are different.

More deals can mean buyers who had waited are now willing to sign. It can also mean sellers finally accepted offers. A busier market is not the same as a more expensive market. The separate Q3 price line was a 0.1% dip, which shows volume and prices can move in different directions.

Buyers should ask which policy the people they are competing with are reacting to, instead of assuming every rule was loosened. Sellers may see more viewings. They should still price from recent sales, because more buyers do not accept every asking price.
facts: EdgeProp: HDB resale transactions rose 19.5% quarter on quarter in Q3 2026
The headline links the jump to policy changes but does not name the rule
19.5% is a change in the number of deals, not in the price index
More sales can happen while prices are flat or slightly down
questions: Does a 19.5% jump in deals mean prices jumped, and should buyers wait?
What did the busier quarter give sellers?
What is the direction when volume rises and the price index does not?
takeaways: The 19.5% is a rise in the number of HDB resale deals in the third quarter of 2026, quarter on quarter. It is not the price index. A buyer who reads it as a 19.5% price jump will misjudge the market. More sales can happen while prices are flat or slightly down. Waiting because volume is high does not buy a cheaper flat. It may mean more listings to choose from. The headline links the jump to policy changes and does not name the rule, so a buyer should not invent which rule to wait out.

Sellers saw a more active quarter. The buyer was more willing to transact than in the previous quarter. That helps a seller with a realistic price. It does not, by itself, justify a new asking price. The future buyer is simply the household that was ready to complete in a busier three months.
The direction is turnover up, price not proven up. A busier market is easier for a fair sale and no help to an ambitious one. Use the 19.5% as a count of deals. Use a price index for price.
n782ad530.description: HDB resale deals jumped 19.5% in Q3 2026. That is more transactions, not a 19.5% rise in prices.
n782ad530.keywords: Singapore property, HDB, resale, transactions, Q3 2026, buyers, sellers, market update, policy

zh.title: 第三季组屋转售成交按季增加19.5%
summary: EdgeProp报道，2026年第三季HDB转售成交按季增加19.5%，并把升幅和政策变化连在一起。标题没有说改的是哪一条规则，也没有说价格涨了19.5%。成交量和价格是两件事。
成交变多，可能是等过的买家现在愿意签约，也可能是卖家终于接受了出价。市场比较忙，不等于市场比较贵。同一季另有价格微跌0.1%的说法，说明成交量和价格可以朝不同方向走。
买家应该问，和你抢房子的人到底在回应哪一条政策，不要假设每条规则都放宽了。卖家可能会看到更多看房。仍然要用近期成交定价，因为买家变多，不代表每一个开价都会被接受。
facts: EdgeProp：2026年第三季组屋转售成交按季增加19.5%
标题把升幅和政策变化连在一起，但没有写出是哪一条规则
19.5%是成交宗数的变化，不是价格指数
成交可以增加，价格同时持平或微跌
questions: 成交跳升19.5%，是不是价钱也跳了，买家该等吗？
更忙的一季给了卖家什么？
成交升、价格指数没有升，方向是什么？
takeaways: 19.5%是2026年第三季组屋转售成交宗数按季的升幅，不是价格指数。把它读成价钱涨了19.5%的买家，会看错市场。成交可以增加，价格同时持平或微跌。因为成交多而等待，等不来更便宜的组屋。它可能只是多了些挂牌可以选择。标题把升幅和政策变化连在一起，但没有写出是哪一条规则，所以买家不该自己编一条规则来等它过去。
卖家看到的是更活跃的一季。买家比上一季更愿意成交。这对开价现实的卖家有帮助。它本身不足以支撑一个新的开价。未来的买家，就是在更忙的三个月里准备完成交易的家庭。
方向是成交上升，价钱没有被证明上升。更忙的市场，对公道的出售更容易，对偏高的开价没有帮助。把19.5%当成成交的宗数。价钱要用价格指数。

summary: Stacked Homes says even the cheapest 4-room HDB flats are not cheap any more, and that flats at S$500,000 have become rare. The headline teases “one statistic” and does not give it. Do not fill that gap with a guess.

S$500,000 can still be a real asking price in some towns and a fantasy in others. Lease, floor and the years left matter as much as the round number. A buyer hunting only for S$500,000 may be looking in the wrong town, or at flats with a short lease.

Sellers in towns where S$500,000 is now low should not assume every 4-room has cleared that bar. Buyers who can pay more should still ask what the extra money buys: a longer lease, a better floor, or simply a hotter estate.
facts: Stacked Homes: S$500,000 4-room HDB flats are described as rare
The headline does not publish the statistic it mentions
S$500,000 is not a national price for every 4-room
Town and remaining lease change what that budget can buy
questions: Should a buyer with $500,000 wait for four-room flats to become common at that price again?
Who can still sell to that budget, and who cannot?
What direction does “rare” describe?
takeaways: Stacked Homes describes a $500,000 four-room flat as rare. Waiting for that budget to become a normal four-room price again is a bet this page does not support. The headline does not publish the statistic behind the claim, so the size of the change should not be invented. Town and remaining lease decide what the budget can still buy. A short lease or a weaker town is how $500,000 still works. A central flat with a long lease is not that flat.

Sellers in stronger towns should not hear “rare” and add a premium regardless of their own stack. The buyer who only has $500,000 is a shrinking group for this flat type. The buyer who clears a four-room in a stronger town is someone who can pay more. A seller in a weaker town, or of a short lease, is who that $500,000 buyer can still reach.

The direction is that the cheaper end of the four-room market has moved up enough to be described as rare at $500,000. That is a level shift in entry stock, not a published percentage. Entry-level buyers need a higher budget, or a town and a lease that the stronger projects no longer offer.
nea3ce065.description: S$500,000 4-room HDB flats are described as rare. Check the town and the lease before you treat that number as the market.
nea3ce065.keywords: Singapore property, HDB, 4-room, resale, S$500,000, buyers, sellers, budget

zh.title: 最便宜的四房组屋也不便宜了，50万新元的单位变少
summary: Stacked Homes说，就算是最便宜的四房组屋也不便宜了，50万新元的单位已经变得少见。标题提起“一个统计”，但没有把数字写出来。不要自己补一个猜测。
50万新元在一些市镇仍可能是真实开价，在另一些市镇则不现实。屋契、楼层和剩余年数，和这个整数一样重要。只找50万新元的买家，可能找错了市镇，或找到的是屋契很短的房子。
在50万新元已经偏低的市镇，卖家也不该假设每一套四房都越过了这条线。付得起更多的买家，仍要问多出来的钱买到了什么：更长的屋契、更好的楼层，还是只是一个更热的邻里。
facts: Stacked Homes：50万新元的四房组屋被形容为少见
标题没有公布它提到的那个统计数字
50万新元不是全岛每一套四房的价钱
市镇和剩余屋契会改变这个预算买得到什么
questions: 预算50万的买家，该不该等四房重新在这个价钱变得常见？
谁还能卖给这个预算，谁不能？
“少见”描述的是什么方向？
takeaways: Stacked Homes把50万新元的四房写成少见。再等这个预算重新变成普通四房的价钱，是这一页没有支持的赌注。标题没有公布它提到的统计，所以变化有多大不该编。市镇和剩余屋契决定这个预算还买得到什么。屋契短，或市镇较弱，50万仍然可能。市中心、屋契长的单位不是那一套。
较强市镇的卖家，不该听见“少见”就不管自己的那一叠、一律加价。只有50万的买家，对这个房型是在变少的一群。在较强市镇买走四房的人，是付得起更多的人。较弱市镇或短屋契的卖家，才是50万的买家还够得到的。
方向是四房较便宜的一端已经上移，50万被写成少见。这是入门货的水平变化，不是一个公布了的百分比。入门买家需要更高的预算，或者一个较强项目已经不再提供的市镇和屋契。

summary: The headline is a commentary: offer owners affected by an en bloc sale some ABSD relief when they buy a replacement home. It is an argument, not a new rule. Nothing in the headline says IRAS has changed additional buyer’s stamp duty.

En bloc sellers are often buying and selling in the same season. Stamp duty on the next home can be large enough to change whether the collective sale still looks attractive. Owners should ask their lawyer what they would pay today, under the rules that exist now.

Buyers who are not in an en bloc should not expect a concession. Sellers voting on a collective sale should put the replacement-home tax in the spreadsheet before they vote. A headline that says “offer” is a suggestion that someone else would still have to pass.
facts: The headline argues for ABSD concessions for owners replacing a home after an en bloc
It does not announce a change in the law or in IRAS rules
ABSD is the extra stamp duty some buyers pay on top of basic duty
The cost of the next home can decide whether an en bloc sum is enough
questions: Should an en bloc owner wait for an ABSD concession?
Who is unaffected, and who has to redo the sums?
What is the direction until the rule actually changes?
takeaways: The headline argues for an additional buyer’s stamp duty concession when an owner has to buy a replacement home after a collective sale. It does not change the law or IRAS rules. An owner who waits for a concession that has not been announced may sit through a sale with today’s tax still due. ABSD is the extra duty on top of basic duty. The cost of the next home decides whether the en bloc proceeds are enough. Waiting does not create a saving that IRAS has not published.

Buyers who are not in a collective sale are unaffected. Sellers in an old condo who are weighing a sale should run the replacement home with today’s ABSD, not with a hoped-for discount. The future buyer of the redeveloped site is a different person from the owner who has to move out. One can wait for the new project. The other needs a home under the current tax.

There is no rule change, so there is no market-wide tax relief. En bloc math stays tight for owners who would pay ABSD on the next home. Until the rule changes, the impact of waiting is uncertainty, not a lower bill.
9770.description: A commentary says en bloc owners should get ABSD relief on a replacement home. That is an argument, not a new rule.
9770.keywords: Singapore property, en bloc, ABSD, condo, sellers, buyers, stamp duty, collective sale

zh.title: 评论：集体出售后换房，应为受影响屋主提供额外买方印花税宽减
summary: 这则标题是一篇评论：集体出售（en bloc）之后要再买房子的屋主，应该在额外买方印花税（ABSD）上得到一些宽减。这是主张，不是新规定。标题并没有说税务局已经修改了额外买方印花税。
集体出售的卖家，常常在同一段时间里又卖又买。下一套房子的印花税，可以大到改变这笔集体出售还算不算划算。屋主应该问律师，按现在已经存在的规则，自己今天要付多少。
不在集体出售里的买家，不要期待有宽减。准备投票的卖家，应该在投票前把下一套房子的税放进表格。标题里的“应该提供”，是一个还要别人通过的建议。
facts: 标题主张，集体出售后换房的屋主应获得额外买方印花税宽减
它没有宣布法律或税务局规则已经改变
额外买方印花税是部分买家在基本印花税之外再付的税
下一套房子的成本，可以决定集体出售的钱够不够
questions: 集体出售的业主该不该等额外买方印花税的宽减？
谁不受影响，谁必须重算？
在规则真正改变之前，方向是什么？
takeaways: 标题主张，集体出售后必须换房的业主应获得额外买方印花税宽减。它没有改变法律，也没有改变税务局的规则。业主如果等一个还没宣布的宽减，可能在出售过程中仍要按今天的税来付。额外买方印花税是基本印花税之外再付的税。下一套房子的成本，决定集体出售的钱够不够。等待不会造出税务局没有公布的省税。
不在集体出售里的买家不受影响。正在考虑出售的旧公寓卖家，该按今天的额外买方印花税来算下一套房子，而不是按一个希望中的折扣。重建后地段的未来买家，和必须搬走的业主不是同一个人。一个可以等新项目。另一个要在现行税制下找房子。
规则没有改，所以没有全市场的税务宽减。对下一套房子要付额外买方印花税的业主，集体出售的账仍然紧。在规则改变之前，等待的影响是不确定，不是一张更低的账单。

summary: Stomp reported that a renovation creator called a 4-room Tengah BTO kitchen one of the most limited layouts he had seen, and that HDB responded. The headline does not quote HDB, and it does not give the kitchen’s measurements. This is a layout argument, not a price.

Tengah buyers choose a flat from a plan, often before they can stand in the finished kitchen. A tight kitchen is a daily problem if you cook. It is also easy to miss when the showflat styling uses smaller furniture. Measure the plan. Ask what is structural and what a contractor can open up.

Sellers of completed Tengah flats will meet buyers who have seen this kind of clip. Be ready to show the real kitchen, not a styled photo. Buyers should not reject an entire town because one stack was criticised, and they should not ignore the plan because the facade looked fine.
facts: Stomp, 19 October 2026: a creator criticised a 4-room Tengah BTO kitchen and HDB responded
The headline does not quote HDB or give measurements
Kitchen layout is a daily-use issue, separate from the town’s price
BTO buyers often decide from floor plans before the flat is built
questions: Should Tengah buyers worry about every 4-room kitchen?
What can you check on a BTO floor plan?
How should a seller answer a buyer who saw the clip?
takeaways: Read the kitchen’s width and length on the plan for the stack you want. One creator’s verdict is not a measurement.
Ask which walls can move and which cannot. A renovation can improve finishes. It cannot always add floor area.
If you are selling a completed flat, let buyers stand in the kitchen. A clip about another stack does not describe yours, and pretending it does not exist will not help.
n01edeaa5.description: A creator criticised a 4-room Tengah BTO kitchen and HDB responded. Buyers should measure the plan, not the clip.
n01edeaa5.keywords: Singapore property, HDB, BTO, Tengah, 4-room, kitchen, renovation, buyers, sellers

zh.title: 装修创作者批评登加四房预购组屋厨房，建屋局作出回应
summary: Stomp报道，一名装修内容创作者把登加（Tengah）一套四房预购组屋的厨房，说成他见过最局促的户型之一，建屋发展局作出了回应。标题没有引用建屋局的原话，也没有厨房的尺寸。这是在讨论户型，不是价钱。
登加的买家常常在厨房还没建好时，就凭图纸选房。如果你常做饭，局促的厨房是每天的问题。示范单位如果用了较小的家具，这一点也很容易被放过。量图纸。问哪些墙是结构墙，承包商能动哪些。
已经建好的登加组屋，卖家会遇到看过这类短片的买家。准备让人看真正的厨房，而不是一张布置过的照片。买家不该因为一个座楼被批评就否定整个市镇，也不该因为外立面好看就忽略图纸。
facts: Stomp，2026年10月19日：创作者批评登加四房预购组屋厨房，建屋局作出回应
标题没有引用建屋局原话，也没有尺寸
厨房户型是日常使用的问题，和市镇价钱是分开的
预购组屋的买家常常在房子建好前就凭平面图决定
questions: 登加的买家是不是该担心每一套四房的厨房？
在预购组屋平面图上可以核对什么？
卖家该怎么回答看过短片的买家？
takeaways: 看你要的那个座楼，厨房在图纸上的宽和长。一位创作者的评价不是尺寸。
问哪些墙可以动，哪些不能。装修可以改饰面，不一定能增加面积。
如果你在卖已经建好的房子，让买家站进厨房。关于另一个座楼的短片描述的不是你的家。假装没有这回事，也没有帮助。

summary: The headline says home buyers are using more cash and CPF savings for down payments. It does not say how the split has changed, or whether prices rose. Cash, CPF and the bank loan are three different pots. Using more of the first two usually means the loan is a smaller share of the price.

That can be a choice, or a requirement. A bigger cash and CPF down payment lowers the monthly repayment. It also leaves less CPF for the next home, and less cash for renovation, stamp duty and the months after you move.

Sellers sometimes hear that buyers are “stretching”. This headline says the opposite pattern: more money up front. Buyers should still write down what is left after the down payment. A purchase that empties both cash and CPF is fragile if income drops.
facts: Headline: buyers are using more cash and CPF savings for down payments
No percentage split is given
Cash, CPF and the bank loan fund a purchase in different ways
A larger down payment cuts the loan and also cuts what is left for the next step
questions: Does a bigger CPF down payment make a home more affordable?
What should be left after the down payment?
What should sellers not assume about buyers’ cash?
takeaways: List cash, CPF and the loan on one page. A larger CPF sum lowers the monthly repayment and also reduces CPF you can use later.
Keep a buffer for stamp duty, legal fees and renovation. A down payment that uses every dollar is not a comfortable purchase.
Sellers should not assume every buyer is stretched, or that every buyer can raise the offer. Ask the structure of the offer, not only the headline price.
9769.description: Buyers are putting more cash and CPF into down payments. A bigger upfront sum lowers the loan and also empties savings.
9769.keywords: Singapore property, HDB, condo, CPF, down payment, buyers, sellers, mortgage

zh.title: 买家用更多现金和公积金支付首期
summary: 标题说，买房的人正在用更多现金和公积金（CPF）储蓄来付首期。它没有说比例改了多少，也没有说房价是否上涨。现金、公积金和银行贷款是三笔不同的钱。前两笔用得更多，通常代表贷款占房价的比例更小。
这可以是选择，也可以是要求。首期里现金和公积金越多，每月供款越低。但下一套房子能用的公积金就更少，装修、印花税和搬进去之后的几个月，现金也更少。
卖家有时听到买家在“硬撑”。这则标题说的是另一种情况：前面先拿出更多钱。买家仍然应该写下首期之后还剩什么。如果现金和公积金一起被掏空，收入一降，这笔购买就很脆。
facts: 标题：买家用更多现金和公积金付首期
没有给出百分比
现金、公积金和银行贷款以不同方式支付房价
首期变大，贷款变小，下一步能用的钱也变少
questions: 用更多公积金付首期，房子就更负担得起吗？
付完首期还应该剩下什么？
卖家不该对买家的现金作什么假设？
takeaways: 把现金、公积金和贷款写在同一页。公积金用得更多，每月供款会下降，以后还能用的公积金也下降。
留一笔给印花税、律师费和装修。把每一块钱都付进首期，不是一笔从容的购买。
卖家不要假设每个买家都在硬撑，也不要假设每个买家都能加价。问出价的结构，不要只看标题上的总价。

summary: The Serra Residences sold less than a quarter of the units it released, at an average of S$3,460 per square foot. “Released” matters. The headline is about the units the developer put out, not necessarily every unit in the project. Less than a quarter of that batch found a buyer.

S$3,460 psf is a high number next to many suburban launches, and it only means something once you know the district and the unit size. A slow first batch is not a failed project, and it is not a bargain, until you see what is left and what those units cost.

Buyers should compare this pace with a fast launch only after the location is clear. Thomson Reserve’s launch weekend was a different project and a different price. Sellers nearby should not assume a slow launch pulls their resale down, or that S$3,460 psf is what buyers will pay for an older flat.
facts: The Serra Residences: less than a quarter of released units sold
Average price reported at S$3,460 psf on those released units
The figure applies to the units released, not automatically to the whole project
The headline does not state the district
questions: Did the whole project sell less than a quarter of its units?
Is S$3,460 psf a price you can compare with any condo?
Does a slow release help nearby resale sellers?
takeaways: Ask how many units were released and how many of those sold. Less than a quarter of a small release is a different story from less than a quarter of the whole project.
Put S$3,460 psf next to the unit size and the district before you decide it is expensive or cheap. Psf without size is not a price you can borrow for.
Do not copy another project’s launch weekend onto this one. Buy the stack in front of you, or price the resale flat you actually own.
9768.description: The Serra Residences sold under a quarter of released units at about S$3,460 psf. Ask what was released before you judge the project.
9768.keywords: Singapore property, condo, new launch, The Serra Residences, psf, buyers, sellers

zh.title: The Serra Residences已推出单位售出不到四分之一，均价每平方英尺3460新元
summary: The Serra Residences已推出的单位，卖出了不到四分之一，平均价格是每平方英尺3460新元。“已推出”这三个字很重要。标题说的是发展商拿出来的那一批，不一定是整个项目的每一套。那一批里，不到四分之一找到了买家。
每平方英尺3460新元，放在许多郊区新盘旁边是高的。但只有知道地区和单位面积，这个数字才有意义。第一批卖得慢，不是项目失败，也不是已经变便宜，除非你看到剩下的是什么、那些单位要多少钱。
买家要把这个速度和卖得很快的新盘比较，应该先弄清地点。汤申珍藏（Thomson Reserve）的开盘周末是另一个项目、另一个价钱。附近的卖家不要假设一个慢热的新盘会拉低自己的转售，也不要假设买家会按每平方英尺3460新元来买一套较旧的房子。
facts: The Serra Residences：已推出单位售出不到四分之一
这批已推出单位的报道均价为每平方英尺3460新元
数字针对已推出的单位，不会自动套到整个项目
标题没有写出地区
questions: 是不是整个项目都卖出了不到四分之一？
每平方英尺3460新元可以拿来和任何公寓比吗？
开盘偏慢，对附近的转售卖家有帮助吗？
takeaways: 先问推出了多少套、其中卖出多少套。一小批里的不到四分之一，和整个项目的不到四分之一，是不同的故事。
把每平方英尺3460新元和单位面积、地区放在一起，再判断贵或便宜。没有面积的每平方英尺，不是你可以拿去贷款的价钱。
不要把另一个项目的开盘周末套到这个项目上。买你眼前的那一套，或给你真正拥有的转售单位定价。

summary: The headline says Good Class Bungalow market activity picked up when pricing was more realistic. A GCB is a landed house in a defined Singapore zone, not a condo and not an ordinary terrace. The headline gives no transaction count and no price.

“Realistic” means buyers and sellers moved closer. It does not say sellers slashed prices, and it does not say buyers overpaid. In this market one house can take months. A pickup in activity is about more serious talks, not a new price list.

Landed buyers should judge the road, the land size and the condition of the house they want. Sellers should look at recent deals on comparable land, not at a mood headline. One busier month does not reprice every GCB.
facts: Headline: GCB activity picked up on more realistic pricing
No deal count or dollar figure is given
A GCB is a landed house, priced by the house and the land
More activity means more serious negotiations, not a published price list
questions: Did GCB prices jump?
What does realistic pricing mean for a seller?
Can a condo owner use this headline?
takeaways: Do not treat a busier GCB market as a higher market. Ask what actually transacted on a similar land size.
Sellers who want a sale have to be near what buyers will sign. A headline that says pricing became realistic is about that gap closing.
Condo and HDB owners should leave this one aside. A landed street does not set the price of a flat.
9762.description: Good Class Bungalow deals picked up when pricing was more realistic. There is no new price in the headline.
9762.keywords: Singapore property, GCB, Good Class Bungalow, landed, buyers, sellers, market update

zh.title: 优质洋房市场在价格更贴近现实后转趋活跃
summary: 标题说，优质洋房（GCB）的市场活动在价格更贴近现实之后转趋活跃。优质洋房是新加坡特定地带的有地住宅，不是公寓，也不是普通的排屋。标题没有成交宗数，也没有价钱。
“更现实”是指买家和卖家的距离拉近了。它没有说卖家大砍价钱，也没有说买家付贵了。这个市场里，一栋房子可以谈几个月。活动增加，说的是认真的洽谈变多，不是出现了一份新的价目表。
有地住宅的买家，应该看路、地的大小，以及想买的那栋房子的状况。卖家应该看相近土地的近期成交，而不是一个气氛标题。忙碌一个月，不会改写每一栋优质洋房的价钱。
facts: 标题：优质洋房在价格更现实后活动增加
没有成交宗数或金额
优质洋房是有地住宅，按房子和土地定价
活动增加指认真洽谈变多，不是公布了价目表
questions: 优质洋房的价格是不是跳涨了？
对卖家来说，价格更现实是什么意思？
公寓屋主可以用这则标题吗？
takeaways: 不要把更忙的优质洋房市场当成更高的价钱。问相近土地实际成交了什么。
想卖掉的人，开价必须接近买家愿意签约的水平。标题说价格变得更现实，说的就是这个差距在缩小。
公寓和组屋的屋主可以把这则放下。一条有地住宅的街，定不了一套组屋的价钱。

summary: New private home sales nearly doubled in September, to 296 units. Nearly double describes the jump from the month before. 296 is the number of new homes sold, not a price, and not the full stock of unsold units.

A month can swing when one project opens its booking. The next month can look quiet if nothing new is released. Buyers should ask which projects made up the 296 before they treat September as a new normal. Sellers of resale condos should ask whether those buyers were choosing a launch instead of an older flat.

The headline does not give a psf figure. A busy booking month does not tell you what a resale unit in your project is worth. It tells you that developer sales had a stronger September than the month before.
facts: New private home sales in September: 296 units
The headline says that was nearly double the previous month
296 is a sales count, not a price per square foot
One project launch can move a monthly total
questions: Did private home prices double in September?
Why can one month look suddenly busy?
What should a resale seller take from 296 sales?
takeaways: Read 296 as new homes sold in September, and “nearly double” as a comparison with the month before. It is not a price increase.
Ask which launches made up the month. A total without the project names is hard to use.
Resale sellers should find out if their buyers also booked a new project. If they did, compete on lease, space and what is already built, not on September’s total.
9758.description: Developers sold 296 new private homes in September, nearly double the month before. That is a sales count, not a price jump.
9758.keywords: Singapore property, new launch, private home, September sales, condo, buyers, sellers, 296 units

zh.title: 9月新建私人住宅销量升至296套，几乎是前一个月的两倍
summary: 9月新建私人住宅的销量升到296套，几乎是前一个月的两倍。“几乎两倍”说的是和上一个月比。296是卖出的新房套数，不是价钱，也不是还没卖掉的全部库存。
如果有一个项目开放预订，单月数字可以突然变大。如果下个月没有新盘推出，数字又可以看起来很静。买家在把9月当成新的常态之前，应该问这296套是哪些项目组成的。转售公寓的卖家应该问，那些买家是不是改去买新盘，而不是买较旧的单位。
标题没有每平方英尺的价钱。预订忙碌的一个月，告诉不了你自己项目里一套转售值多少。它只说明发展商的销量在9月比前一个月强。
facts: 9月新建私人住宅销量：296套
标题说这几乎是前一个月的两倍
296是销量，不是每平方英尺的价钱
一个项目开盘就可以带动单月总数
questions: 9月私人住宅的价格是不是翻倍了？
为什么单月会突然变忙？
转售卖家该从296套销量里拿走什么？
takeaways: 把296读成9月卖出的新房套数，把“几乎两倍”读成和前一个月的比较。这不是价格上涨。
问这个月是哪些新盘组成的。没有项目名称的总数，很难用。
转售卖家应该弄清买家有没有同时订了新盘。如果有，就在屋契、空间和房子已经建好这几点上比较，而不是用9月的总数。

summary: EL Development was the only bidder for the Marina Gardens Lane site, at S$450 million, or S$1,243 per square foot per plot ratio. A sole bid means nobody else put in a tender. Psf ppr is the land price spread over the floor area the site is allowed to build. It is not the future condo’s selling price.

The launch price, when there is one, has to cover construction and financing on top of that land. Buyers cannot book a unit from a tender result. Sellers in the area should not add S$1,243 psf to their resale and call it the new market.

A single bidder can mean developers were cautious about that site. It can also simply mean one developer wanted it and others did not. The headline does not say the bid was above or below forecasts. Use the two figures as land cost, and wait for a project name before you compare homes.
facts: EL Development: sole bid for Marina Gardens Lane
Bid: S$450 million, or S$1,243 psf ppr
Psf ppr is land price over allowed floor area, not a unit’s selling price
A sole bid means one tender, not a sold condo
questions: Is S$1,243 psf what a future unit will cost?
What does a sole bid tell buyers?
Should nearby resale prices move by the land bid?
takeaways: Keep S$450 million and S$1,243 psf ppr in the land column. Do not quote them as a condo price.
There is no unit to buy until a project is launched. Keep shopping among homes that have a price list.
Nearby sellers should wait for that launch price, then compare like for like. A tender result is not a valuation of an existing flat.
9757.description: EL Development’s sole bid for Marina Gardens Lane was S$450 million, or S$1,243 psf of floor area. That is land cost, not a unit price.
9757.keywords: Singapore property, land bid, Marina Gardens Lane, psf ppr, new launch, condo, EL Development, buyers, sellers

zh.title: 永联发展以4.5亿新元独资标得滨海花园径地段，折合楼面地价每平方英尺1243新元
summary: 永联发展（EL Development）是滨海花园径（Marina Gardens Lane）地段唯一的投标者，出价4.5亿新元，折合每平方英尺楼面地价1243新元。唯一投标，就是没有第二份标书。楼面地价是把地价分摊到这块地允许建造的楼面面积。它不是将来公寓的售价。
真的开盘时，售价还要盖上建筑和融资。买家不能凭招标结果预订单位。这一带的卖家也不该把每平方英尺1243新元加到自己的转售价上，然后称之为新的市价。
只有一个投标者，可以代表发展商对这块地比较谨慎，也可以只是一家想要、其他家不要。标题没有说这口价高于还是低于预测。把这两个数字当成地价，等有了项目名称，再拿来和房子比较。
facts: 永联发展：滨海花园径地段的唯一投标
出价：4.5亿新元，或每平方英尺楼面地价1243新元
楼面地价是地价分摊到允许建造的面积，不是单位售价
唯一投标是一次土地招标，不是一套已经卖出的公寓
questions: 每平方英尺1243新元是将来一套单位的价钱吗？
只有一个投标者，对买家说明了什么？
附近的转售价该不该跟着土地出价移动？
takeaways: 把4.5亿新元和每平方英尺1243新元的楼面地价留在地价那一栏。不要把它们说成公寓售价。
项目还没推出之前，没有可以买的单位。继续看已经有价目表的房子。
附近的卖家应等开盘价，再做同类比较。一次招标结果，不是现有房子的估价。

summary: EdgeProp reported a fresh record at Amber Park, a freehold condo in District 15, at S$3,170 per square foot. A project record is the highest psf that project has achieved, not the price of every unit there, and not the price of every condo in Katong or the east.

Freehold is part of why buyers pay up. The headline does not say the unit’s size, floor or view. A small unit can print a high psf while a larger unit in the same project costs more in dollars and less per foot. Ask which one set the record.

Sellers in Amber Park should not add a premium unless their unit is comparable. Sellers in leasehold projects nearby should not copy S$3,170 at all. Buyers should decide if freehold in District 15 is what they are paying for, then check the loan on the actual price, not only the psf.
facts: EdgeProp: Amber Park, a freehold District 15 condo, hit S$3,170 psf
Described as a fresh record for that project
The headline does not give the unit size or floor
A project record is not a district-wide price
questions: Does S$3,170 psf apply to every Amber Park unit?
Should a leasehold condo nearby use this number?
What is missing before you can judge the record?
takeaways: Ask the size and the floor of the unit that hit S$3,170 psf. Psf without size can flatter a small stack.
Compare freehold with freehold. A leasehold flat down the road is a different product, even in the same district.
Work from the dollar price and the monthly loan. A record psf is a headline. The loan is the bill.
nd6c085c3.description: Amber Park in District 15 set a project record at S$3,170 psf. Ask the unit size before you treat it as the east’s price.
nd6c085c3.keywords: Singapore property, condo, Amber Park, District 15, freehold, psf, resale, buyers, sellers

zh.title: 第15区永久地契公寓Amber Park创下每平方英尺3170新元的项目新高
summary: EdgeProp报道，第15区永久地契公寓Amber Park创下每平方英尺3170新元的新高。项目纪录是这个项目到过的最高每平方英尺价钱，不是这里每一套单位的价钱，也不是加东或整个东部每一栋公寓的价钱。
永久地契是买家愿意多付的原因之一。标题没有说单位面积、楼层或景观。小单位可以打出很高的每平方英尺，同一项目里更大的单位总价更高、每平方英尺却更低。先问是哪一套创的纪录。
Amber Park的卖家，除非单位真的可比，否则不该自己加价。附近租赁地契项目的卖家，更不该照抄3170新元。买家要先决定，自己付的是不是第15区的永久地契，然后按实际总价算贷款，不要只看每平方英尺。
facts: EdgeProp：第15区永久地契公寓Amber Park达到每平方英尺3170新元
被形容为该项目的新高
标题没有给出单位面积或楼层
项目纪录不是整个区的价钱
questions: 每平方英尺3170新元适用于Amber Park的每一套吗？
附近的租赁地契公寓该用这个数字吗？
判断这宗纪录之前还缺什么？
takeaways: 问创下每平方英尺3170新元的那一套有多大、在几楼。没有面积的每平方英尺，会让小单位看起来特别高。
永久地契和永久地契比。同一区里一套租赁地契的房子，是另一种产品。
从总价和每月供款算起。纪录的每平方英尺是标题。贷款才是账单。

summary: The headline says HDB resale prices have fallen for three straight quarters, and asks whether you should buy or wait. Three quarters of declines is the claim. The headline does not say how much each quarter fell. A long slide of tiny moves is not the same as a sharp drop.

Waiting has a cost. Rent, a wedding, a child or a lease running down does not pause because the index might fall a bit more. Buying also has a cost: the flat you pick, at today’s price, with today’s loan. The right question is which cost you can carry, not which quarter looks clever.

Sellers who hold on for a rebound should know the index has already had three softer quarters. That does not mean the fourth must fall, and it does not mean your block has fallen with the index. Buyers who wait should name a price and a date. “Wait” without either is just delay.
facts: Headline claim: HDB resale prices fell for three straight quarters
The headline does not give the size of each quarterly move
It poses a choice: buy now or wait
The index is not the price of one flat
questions: Should HDB buyers wait for a fourth down quarter?
Have all flats fallen because the index has?
What should a seller do after three softer quarters?
takeaways: Do not wait for a bottom you cannot date. If the flat and the loan work now, three small quarterly moves may not be worth another year of rent.
Check your town, not only the national line. A flat can hold its price while the index inches down.
Sellers should look at offers in hand. Holding out is reasonable only if you can name what you are waiting for, and you can afford the wait.
9752.description: HDB resale prices have fallen for three straight quarters. Buy or wait based on the flat and the loan, not on timing the bottom.
9752.keywords: Singapore property, HDB, resale, buyers, sellers, timing, market update, prices

zh.title: 组屋转售价已连跌三个季度，现在买还是再等？
summary: 标题说，HDB转售价已经连跌三个季度，并问你该现在买还是再等。连跌三个季度是这则标题的说法。它没有写出每一季跌了多少。一连串很小的下跌，和一次明显的下跌，不是同一件事。
等待是有成本的。租金、结婚、孩子，或屋契一天天变短，不会因为指数也许还会再跌一点就暂停。买也有成本：你选的那套房子、今天的价钱、今天的贷款。该问的是你承担得起哪一种成本，不是哪一个季度看起来更聪明。
想撑到反弹的卖家，要知道指数已经软了三个季度。这不代表第四季一定再跌，也不代表你的座楼跟着指数跌了。想等的买家应该写出一个价钱和一日期。“再等等”如果两样都没有，就只是拖延。
facts: 标题的说法：组屋转售价连跌三个季度
标题没有给出每一季的跌幅
它提出一个选择：现在买，还是再等
指数不是一套房子的价钱
questions: 组屋买家该不该再等第四个下跌的季度？
指数跌了，是不是所有房子都跌了？
连软三个季度之后，卖家该怎么做？
takeaways: 不要等一个你写不出日期的底部。如果房子和贷款现在就成立，三个很小的季度变动，未必值得再付一年租金。
看你的市镇，不要只看全岛那一条线。指数微跌时，一套房子仍可能守住价钱。
卖家应该看手上的出价。继续等，只有在你说得出在等什么，而且等得起的时候，才算合理。

summary: VnExpress reported that a freehold bungalow tied to a late Singapore property tycoon has been put up for sale at nearly $65 million. “Put on sale” means an asking price. It is not a completed deal. The headline does not name the road.

Nearly $65 million is one house, on freehold land, with a well-known former owner. It does not move the price of a condo or an HDB flat. Landed buyers who are not shopping at that level can ignore the number. Sellers of ordinary landed homes should not add a zero because a trophy house is listed.

Until there is a buyer and a price that was actually paid, this is a listing. Trophy listings can sit. They can also sell quickly if the price meets a buyer who wants that exact house. Neither outcome is a signal for the rest of the market.
facts: VnExpress: a late tycoon’s freehold bungalow is on sale at nearly $65 million
That is an asking price, not a reported sale
The headline does not name the address
One trophy listing does not price condos or HDB flats
questions: Has the bungalow sold for nearly $65 million?
Should other landed sellers follow that asking price?
Does this listing matter to HDB or condo owners?

summary: PropertyNet.SG put District 5 condo prices for 2026 this way: about S$1,913 psf for resale and about S$2,379 psf for a new launch in Pasir Panjang. The gap is the story. A new project asks more per foot than the resale stock the headline is using.

The higher psf can buy a fresh lease, new facilities and a developer’s price list. The lower psf can buy a larger older flat, a tenant already in place, or a lease that has already started to run. The headline does not name the projects. You cannot tell which building is the S$1,913 and which is the S$2,379 until you read the note behind it.

Buyers in Pasir Panjang should compare dollar price and size, not only psf. A cheaper psf on a big old unit can still be the larger loan. Sellers of older condos should show what the buyer saves against the new launch, in dollars and in space, instead of arguing about which psf is fair.

summary: Business Times reported that the Canberra Drive executive condo site drew 13 bids. The top offer was S$825 per square foot per plot ratio, from a Santarli-led joint venture, and it was described as a record. Business Times also described it as the first EC land tender since new rules.

S$825 psf ppr is what the developer bid for the land, spread over the floor area that can be built. It is not the price a family will pay for an EC unit. That price comes later, after construction costs are added, and only households who qualify can buy an executive condo.

Thirteen bidders means more than one developer wanted EC land in that part of Sembawang. It does not mean you can apply this month. Upgraders from an HDB flat should watch for the project name and the launch price, and check the income ceiling and the resale rules before they treat a land record as their future home’s value.

zh.title: 堪培拉通道执行共管公寓地段收到13份标书，最高楼面地价每平方英尺825新元
summary: 《商业时报》报道，堪培拉通道（Canberra Drive）的执行共管公寓（EC）地段收到13份标书。最高出价是每平方英尺楼面地价825新元，来自三塔利（Santarli）牵头的合资公司，并被形容为纪录。《商业时报》也把它写成新规则之后的第一块执行共管公寓土地招标。
每平方英尺825新元的楼面地价，是发展商为土地出的价，分摊到可以建造的楼面面积。它不是一个家庭将来买执行共管公寓单位要付的价钱。那个价钱要等建筑成本加上去之后才出现，而且只有符合资格的家庭才能买。
13个投标者，代表不止一家发展商想要三巴旺这一带的执行共管公寓用地。这不代表你这个月可以申请。准备从组屋升级的人，应该等项目名称和开盘价，并在把一个土地纪录当成未来房子的价值之前，先核对收入顶限和转售规则。

最高出价：三塔利牵头的合资公司，每平方英尺楼面地价825新元，被形容为纪录
被写成新规则之后的第一块执行共管公寓土地招标
这个数字是地价，不是执行共管公寓单位的售价

土地招标结束了，买家现在可以申请吗？
土地出价创纪录，对组屋升级者意味着什么？

你不能凭一则招标标题预订这套执行共管公寓。等开盘，再核对你的家庭够不够资格。
投标人多，说明发展商想要这块地。它告诉不了你一套还没开卖的房子，每月贷款是多少。

summary: The Straits Times carried this Singapore property headline: Luxury homes seized in $3b money laundering case prove a hard sell. The headline gives these figures: $3. The notes below are for buyers and sellers. They are not a copy of the original article.

Buyers should check this headline against the home, the location and the monthly cost they can live with. Ask what the number refers to: a land bid, a transacted resale price, an asking price, or a whole-market move.

Sellers should answer questions about their own unit. One market headline is not a valuation. If you are timing a sale or an HDB upgrade, use the figure as a question to research, then confirm it on the official data or the listing itself.
facts: Source named on this page: The Straits Times
Headline: Luxury homes seized in $3b money laundering case prove a hard sell
Figure in the headline: $3
takeaways: Waiting can bring more of this stock, but it has been slow. Since 17 September, 47 properties were auctioned and five sold. The New Futura unit went for $8.5 million on a single bid, 13% under a $9.8 million guide, and $500,000 above a similar-sized unit in the project that sold for $8 million in July 2025. A buyer who wants a forced-sale discount is looking at a thin, slow clearance. A buyer who needs a home on a normal timetable should not plan around the next CAD auction.

These prices belong to seized homes, liquidated by Deloitte, with 60% additional buyer’s stamp duty still on foreign buyers and cheaper new prime launches as the alternative. SRI sold five of 16. Edmund Tie’s only bid on 23 September was an 8,880-square-foot Kaki Bukit factory, above $3.2 million, after private talks. A willing seller of a freehold city apartment is not that seller. Matching a liquidation price gives away the difference between a forced sale and a sale the owner can refuse.

The direction is heavy at the seized end of the prime market. More than half of the 80-plus seized properties have already been offered. The report expects Sentosa Cove to be harder still, because buyers can choose freehold city units that are easier to resell. Suburban homes and HDB flats are outside this trade. Waiting does not pull their prices down with the auctions.
questions: Those seized homes are already hard to sell. What home of yours are you still waiting to price?
A difficult luxury sale does not view your flat for you. When is your next viewing?
Who is shopping in your price range this week, while these homes sit?

summary: The Straits Times报道了这则新加坡房地产标题：涉30亿元洗钱案被扣押的豪宅难以出售。下面的说明是写给买家和卖家的，不是原文照搬。
买房的人要把标题里的数字，拿来和实际的房子、地段、剩余屋契和每月供款比较。先问清楚数字指的是地价、成交价、开价，还是整个市场的变动。
卖房的人不要把一条标题直接套到自己的单位上。准备出售或从组屋升级时，把数字当成要去核实的问题，再对照官方数据或真实挂牌。
facts: 本页来源：The Straits Times
标题：涉30亿元洗钱案被扣押的豪宅难以出售
标题中的数字：$3
takeaways: 再等，可能会有更多这类货，但出清很慢。9月17日以来拍卖了47个物业，卖掉五个。New Futura那套以850万新元成交，只有一个出价，比980万的指导价低13%，又比2025年7月同项目一套面积相近、以800万成交的单位高50万。想要法拍折扣的人，面对的是一批少而慢的货。按正常时间要房子的人，不该把计划押在下一场商业事务局的拍卖上。
这些价钱属于被扣押、由德勤清算的房子。外国买家仍要付60%的额外买方印花税，也可以改买更便宜的黄金地段新盘。SRI卖掉16个里的五个。戴德梁行9月23日九个出价里唯一成交的，是经私下洽谈、以超过320万新元卖掉的加基武吉8880平方英尺厂房。自愿出售市中心永久地契公寓的人，不是这种卖家。把开价降到清算价，让掉的是被迫出售和卖家可以拒绝之间的差价。
方向是被扣押豪宅这一端偏重。80多个被扣押物业里，超过一半已经拿出来拍卖。报道认为圣淘沙湾会更难卖，因为买家可以改选更好转手的市中心永久地契。郊区私宅和组屋不在这笔交易里。再等，也不会把它们的价钱一起拉低。

keypoints: 里恩尼山路New Futura的一个永久地契单位，业主是30亿元洗钱案嫌疑人王炳刚的妻子。它在10月28日的拍卖中以850万新元成交。
这个2691平方英尺的单位，成交价比980万新元的指导价低13%，也比2025年7月同项目一套相近面积、以800万新元成交的单位高出50万新元。
只有一个出价。自9月17日以来送拍的47个物业里，这是第五个卖出的。
另外四套公寓在Wallich Residence和Martin Modern，于9月23日成交，合计1628万新元。
商业事务局查封的80多个物业里，超过一半已经送去拍卖。
德勤负责清理这些资产。受委的三家经纪行里，只有两家有成交。
SRI卖出16个物业中的5个。Edmund Tie在私下洽谈后，以超过320万新元卖出加基武吉一座8880平方英尺的工厂。9月23日它推出的9个物业里，只有这座工厂有人出价。
指导价高、外国买家60%的额外买方印花税，以及黄金地段更便宜的新盘，都在压制需求。
报道说圣淘沙湾的房子可能更难卖，因为买家可以选择市中心更容易转手的永久地契单位。
A freehold unit at New Futura on Leonie Hill Road, owned by the wife of Wang Bingang, a suspect in the $3 billion money-laundering case, sold at auction on 28 October for $8.5 million.
The price was 13% under the $9.8 million guide for the 2,691-square-foot apartment, and $500,000 above an $8 million sale of a similar-sized unit in the project in July 2025.
It drew a single bid. It is the fifth property to sell out of 47 put on auction since 17 September.
Four other apartments, at Wallich Residence and Martin Modern, sold on 23 September for $16.28 million in total.
More than half of the 80-plus properties seized by the Commercial Affairs Department have been put up for auction.
Deloitte is liquidating the assets. Only two of the three appointed brokerages have recorded sales.

SRI sold five of its 16 properties. Edmund Tie sold an 8,880-square-foot factory in Kaki Bukit for above $3.2 million after private talks. That factory was the only one of nine it offered on 23 September to draw a bid.
High guide prices, the 60% additional buyer’s stamp duty on foreign buyers, and cheaper new launches in prime districts are weighing on demand.
The report says Sentosa Cove homes may be harder to sell, because buyers can choose freehold city units that are easier to resell.

summary: Real Estate Asia carried this Singapore property headline: Singapore HDB resale prices forecast to grow up to 1% in 2026. The headline gives these figures: 1%. The notes below are for buyers and sellers. They are not a copy of the original article.

HDB buyers should compare the headline with the actual flat, the remaining lease, the town and the monthly mortgage. Ask what the number refers to: a land bid, a transacted resale price, an asking price, or a whole-market move.

HDB sellers should not copy one headline price onto their own block. Buyers will ask about floor, lease and condition. If you are timing a sale or an HDB upgrade, use the figure as a question to research, then confirm it on the official data or the listing itself.
facts: Source named on this page: Real Estate Asia
Headline: Singapore HDB resale prices forecast to grow up to 1% in 2026
Figure in the headline: 1%
takeaways: A buyer waiting for a fall is waiting against a forecast of 0% to 1% growth for 2026, revised from a range that ran from a 1% fall to 2% growth. That is flat to slightly up, not a sale. The reason to wait is supply, not a called crash. Flats finishing their minimum occupation period are forecast at 13,484 in 2026 and 18,939 in 2027, against 6,973 in 2025. More of those flats on the market is more choice. It is not a stated discount.

Sellers of larger and premium flats may still meet private owners who are moving to something more practical. That buyer can keep million-dollar deals active in some areas. Realion does not expect that demand to lift the whole market. A seller of an ordinary flat who prices off the premium end is aiming at a buyer who is not theirs. The cash buyer of a large flat and the loan buyer of a standard flat are different people.

The direction into 2027 is steadier broad prices, with a much larger pool of flats coming out of the occupation period. The top can stay busy while the index moves inside 1%. Waiting through that is a choice about selection, not about catching a drop the forecast does not contain.
questions: The 2026 range is already published. What flat are you still hoping will get cheaper first?
More flats leave the occupation period each year. Which of today’s listings will still be there?

facts: 本页来源：PropertyNet.SG
标题：2026年家居改进计划（HIP）前卖还是后卖：工程约18个月，住户家中约10个工作日
takeaways: 投票通过后，整个项目大约18个月，屋子里的工程大约10个工作日。只有买家愿意为做完的可选项目付出比屋契更多的钱，这个等待才划算。很多够资格做计划的旧组屋，屋契更要紧，因为全额贷款和全额公积金住房补助，要求屋契覆盖最年轻的买家到95岁。标准组屋已满五年最低居住年限的业主，工程进行期间也可以卖。为了升级抱着不卖，最后遇到拿不到全额贷款的买家，是昂贵的等法。
按2026年5月15日的安排，公民家庭的基本工程由政府支付，可选项目按房型自付5%至12.5%。六个星期的选择期内，买卖双方要用书面约定谁向建屋局提交选择。投票前，由当时的业主选。买家不把这一点锁死，买到的是别人的装修清单。未来的买家，仍是受得了剩余屋契的家庭。
家居改进是维修周期，不是涨势。它没有说组屋价钱在涨。这些旧组屋的方向仍由屋契和贷款决定，升级只是上面的一个小调整。
questions: 投票通过后工程大约18个月，屋子里大约10个工作日。你的出售等得起吗？
更在意屋契、而不是新配件的买家，现在就在找。18个月后他们还在吗？
你等可选工程做完的时候，哪一套还没卖掉？
keypoints: 建屋局的家居改进计划手册说，投票通过后，一个典型项目大约要18个月。个别单位里面的工程通常大约10个工作日。
新加坡公民家庭的必要改进由政府支付。自选改进由屋主付5%至12.5%，按房型而定。这是建屋局2026年5月15日宣布的。
只要已满最低居住年限，工程进行期间也可以卖。标准组屋的年限是五年。
谁来选自选项目，要看卖出的时间。投票前，由当时的屋主选。在六个星期的选择期内，买卖双方应书面说好，并向建屋局确认由谁提交选择。
若要等整个项目完工才卖，可能要多持有大约18个月，换来的只是单位内大约10个工作日的工程。
对许多已经符合计划屋龄的组屋，买家往往更在意剩余屋契，而不是翻新本身。因为全额贷款和全额公积金购屋津贴，取决于屋契能否让最年轻的买家住到95岁。
HDB’s Home Improvement Programme booklet says a typical project takes about 18 months after a successful poll, while the work inside one flat usually takes about 10 working days.

For Singapore-citizen households, the Government pays for the essential improvements. Owners pay 5% to 12.5% of the optional improvements, depending on flat type, under HDB’s 15 May 2026 announcement.
A flat can be sold while the works are going on, once the minimum occupation period has been met. For a Standard flat that period is five years.

Who chooses the optional items depends on the timing. Before the poll, it is the owner then. During the six-week selection window, seller and buyer should agree in writing and confirm with HDB who submits the choices.
Waiting for the whole project to finish can mean holding the flat for about 18 months, for roughly 10 working days of work inside the unit.

For many flats old enough for the programme, the remaining lease often matters more to buyers than the upgrade, because the full loan and the full CPF housing grant depend on the lease lasting the youngest buyer to age 95.

The likely buyer of this fifth-floor three-bedroom duplex is an owner-occupier who wants the space, not a buyer hunting a forced discount.

takeaways: It is not a reason to delay a purchase. The flat’s location was not named, so no town is marked down. The first entry was during an air-conditioner installation, with the door open, in late July, while the BTO flat was being renovated. The cost of waiting to fit a camera and to keep the door controlled was a second visit five days later, with a woman, behind Building Service Centre workers. Owners who are mid-renovation should treat an empty flat as unsecured. That is the action. It is not a valuation.

A seller handing over a flat that is still being renovated should expect the buyer’s worry to be access, not the town’s headline price. The owners in this account confronted the pair through the CCTV speaker, and they have not returned. A future buyer of a new flat should budget for a lock and a camera before the works start, and should not leave the door open for trades.
There is no market direction. Future buyers of new flats are not paying less because of one unnamed incident. The impact sits with households who have keys and have not moved in.

facts: 本页来源：8days.sg
标题：Man Trespasses S'pore Couple's 预购组屋组屋 Twice, Brings Wife Second Visit
takeaways: 这不是推迟购买的理由。地点没有公布，所以没有任何市镇被压价。第一次进入是7月下旬装空调、门开着的时候，预购组屋正在装修。等着不装摄像头、不看住门的代价，是五天后的第二次，一名女子跟着大厦服务中心的工作人员进来。正在装修的业主，该把空屋子当成没有防备。这是要做的事，不是估价。
交房时工程还在进行的卖家，该预期买家担心的是进出，不是市镇的标题价钱。这个例子里的屋主通过闭路电视扬声器对上了那两人，之后他们没有再来。新组屋的未来买家，该在工程开始前就预算一把锁和一个摄像头，也不该为了施工把门开着。
没有市场方向。未来的新组屋买家，不会因为一次没有点名的事件而少付钱。影响落在已经拿了钥匙、还没搬进去的家庭。
questions: 这发生在一套装修中的房子。你自己的房子，这个星期有没有没锁好？
转售的买家是在拿钥匙之后才见到房子。你约了哪一场看房？
你已经选中的那套房子，还有什么一直没做？
keypoints: 一对新加坡夫妇说，7月下旬他们的预购组屋正在装修时，一名男子两次进入单位。他们没有公布地点。
他们把经过发在Instagram账号@navigatethirty。
第一次是在安装空调、门开着的时候。那名男子似乎四处看并拍照，然后注意到闭路电视。
五天后，他跟着大厦服务中心的工作人员，和一名女子再次进入单位。
屋主通过闭路电视的扬声器和他们说话。这两人之后没有再来。
A Singapore couple said a man entered their BTO flat twice in late July, while it was being renovated. They did not name the location.
They posted the account on Instagram under @navigatethirty.
The first time, the door was open for an air-conditioner installation. The man appeared to look around and take photos, then noticed the CCTV.
Five days later he returned with a woman, following Building Service Centre workers into the flat.
The owners spoke to the pair through the CCTV speaker. The pair have not returned.

summary: 99.co carried this Singapore property headline: Tampines executive flat sells for record S$1.275M, becoming the town’s second priciest HDB resale. The headline gives these figures: S$1.275M. The notes below are for buyers and sellers. They are not a copy of the original article.

HDB buyers should compare the headline with the actual flat, the remaining lease, the town and the monthly mortgage. Ask what the number refers to: a land bid, a transacted resale price, an asking price, or a whole-market move.

HDB sellers should not copy one headline price onto their own block. Buyers will ask about floor, lease and condition. If you are timing a sale or an HDB upgrade, use the figure as a question to research, then confirm it on the official data or the listing itself.
facts: Source named on this page: 99.co
Headline: Tampines executive flat sells for record S$1.275M, becoming the town’s second priciest HDB resale
Figure in the headline: S$1.275M
takeaways: Waiting has not been producing cheaper executive flats at the top of Tampines. This sale is $1.275 million, about $834 per square foot, for 1,528 square feet on storeys 7 to 9. It is 76 square feet smaller than the June record and about seven years shorter on the lease, and it is still $35,000 higher. A buyer who waits for size and lease to be rewarded is waiting against what this print just did.

The lease began in 1988, so about 61 years remained. A younger buyer who needs the lease to cover them to 95 may not get a full loan or the full CPF grant on this flat, even at a record price. That shrinks the future buyer to an older household, or one paying with more cash. Sellers of the large executive stock can show the record. Sellers of the flats that have been trading at $1.2 million to $1.21 million should not assume the whole band moved by 2.8%.

The direction is firm at the very top of Tampines executive resale, and ordinary above that band. Two sales, this one and the June sale at $1.24 million, sit above a cluster of four between $1.2 million and $1.21 million. It is a niche. It should not be copied onto a four-room flat in the town.
questions: One Tampines executive flat set a mark. Does your flat share its floor, lease and size?
The next buyer of a large Tampines flat is reading this too. Are you ready to meet them?
What would another week of waiting tell you that this sale has not already shown?

facts: 本页来源：99.co
标题：淡滨尼 executive 组屋 sells 纪录 S$1.275M, becoming town’s second priciest 组屋转售
标题中的数字：S$1.275M
takeaways: 再等，并没有等来淡滨尼顶端更便宜的公寓式组屋。这一笔是127万5000新元，约每平方英尺834新元，1528平方英尺，7至9楼。它比6月的纪录小76平方英尺，屋契大约短七年，价钱仍高3万5000新元。想等面积和屋契得到回报的人，等的方向和这笔成交相反。
屋契从1988年起，大约还剩61年。较年轻的买家如果需要屋契覆盖到95岁，就算这是纪录价，也可能拿不到全额贷款或全额公积金补助。未来的买家因此缩成较年长的家庭，或现金较多的人。大型公寓式组屋的卖家可以出示这个纪录。成交落在120万至121万的卖家，不该假设整个价带都涨了2.8%。
方向是淡滨尼公寓式组屋的最顶端稳，过了那一档就普通。这一笔和6月的124万，高于四笔120万至121万的成交。这是一个小众。不该抄到同市镇的四房式上。
questions: 淡滨尼有一套公寓式组屋标出了一个高点。你的房子有同样的楼层、屋契和面积吗？
下一位置换淡滨尼大单位的人也在看这篇。你准备好见他们了吗？
再等一个星期，能告诉你什么是这宗成交还没显示的？

这是淡滨尼行政公寓的新纪录，也是全镇各类组屋转售里的第二高价。
单位1528平方英尺，三间卧室，位于7楼至9楼。价格大约每平方英尺834新元。
屋契从1988年开始，大约还剩61年。
之前的行政公寓纪录是淡滨尼82街第856F座一个1604平方英尺的单位，2026年6月以124万新元成交，约每平方英尺773新元。当时屋契大约还剩68年。
新纪录的面积少了76平方英尺，屋契大约短七年，价格却高出3万5000新元，约2.8%。两套都在7楼至9楼。

以1528平方英尺计算，它是被比较的七宗高价交易里面积最小的，价格却是第二高。
An executive flat at Block 938 Tampines Avenue 5, in Tampines Palmspring, sold for $1.275 million in November 2026.
That is a new record for an executive flat in Tampines, and the town’s second-highest HDB resale of any type.
The home is 1,528 square feet, with three bedrooms, on the 7th to 9th storeys. The price is about $834 per square foot.
The lease began in 1988, so about 61 years remained.
The previous executive record was a 1,604-square-foot flat at Block 856F Tampines Street 82, sold for $1.24 million, or $773 per square foot, in June 2026. About 68 years were left on that lease.
The new record is 76 square feet smaller, about seven years shorter on the lease, and $35,000 higher, about 2.8%. Both flats are on the 7th to 9th storeys.
Of the recent executive sales at or above $1.2 million in Tampines, four were between $1.2 million and $1.21 million. This sale and the June sale are the ones above that band.
At 1,528 square feet it was the smallest of the seven high sales being compared, and the second-highest price.

summary: Tatler Asia carried this Singapore property headline: Home tour: how Peter Tay breathes new soul into a Good Class Bungalow once owned by a Singapore president. The notes below are for buyers and sellers. They are not a copy of the original article.

Landed buyers should treat one address as one house. The land size, the road and the price have to be checked on that property. Ask what the number refers to: a land bid, a transacted resale price, an asking price, or a whole-market move.

Landed sellers should not move their asking price just because another bungalow was in the news. If you are timing a sale or an HDB upgrade, use the figure as a question to research, then confirm it on the official data or the listing itself.
facts: Source named on this page: Tatler Asia
Headline: Home tour: how Peter Tay breathes new soul into a Good Class Bungalow once owned by a Singapore president
takeaways: No. There is no sale and no asking price. Waiting or buying has to be decided on a real house, a real plot and a real cheque. This is a design tour of a Swettenham Road bungalow whose interiors took about two and a half years, beside a new shell by Kevin Tan of Akta-rchitects. Paying up, or holding off, because a magazine walked through a finished house is not an investment decision.

The client was a food entrepreneur housing a family of six: the couple, three children and his mother-in-law. That is the buyer of this kind of work, someone who can fund a multi-year interior on a Good Class Bungalow plot of at least about 15,070 square feet. A seller can use the tour to show the finish this tier expects. An unrenovated house does not become worth the finished one.

The article does not say whether Good Class Bungalow prices are rising or falling. It shows demand for bespoke completed houses among owners who can pay for time. A claim that a president once owned the house is not part of this tour and should not be added to the value.
questions: This is one finished house. What house were you already planning to walk through?
A design visit does not book the bungalow for you. When is your viewing?
If the home you want is on the market, what are you still collecting pictures of?

facts: 本页来源：Tatler Asia
标题：住宅 tour: how Peter Tay breathes soul 优质洋房 once owned 新加坡 president
takeaways: 没有。没有成交，也没有开价。买或等，要落在一栋真实的房子、一块真实的地和一张真实的支票上。这是史勿登路一栋洋房的设计参观，室内做了大约两年半，新的建筑外壳出自Akta-rchitects的Kevin Tan。因为一本杂志走了一圈成品屋就加价或按兵不动，不是投资决定。

如果你要的房子已经在卖，你还在收集谁的照片？

优质洋房（Good Class Bungalow）坐落在指定地段，地皮至少15070平方英尺。

The house was commissioned by a food entrepreneur for a family of six: the couple, their three children and his mother-in-law.

summary: Borneo Bulletin carried this Singapore property headline: Singapore explores build-to-rent model as demand for independent living grows. The notes below are for buyers and sellers. They are not a copy of the original article.

Renters who want to buy later should set the rent next to what they can still save each month for an HDB flat or a condo. Ask what the number refers to: a land bid, a transacted resale price, an asking price, or a whole-market move.

Landlords should price against what tenants can pay, not against a headline about a new rental idea. If you are timing a sale or an HDB upgrade, use the figure as a question to research, then confirm it on the official data or the listing itself.
facts: Source named on this page: Borneo Bulletin
Headline: Singapore explores build-to-rent model as demand for independent living grows
takeaways: Waiting for a build-to-rent flat to replace a purchase is waiting without a date. The Ministry of National Development still puts home ownership at the centre. Build-to-rent, co-living and long-stay serviced apartments are being looked at for people who want their own place before they buy, or who are here to work or study. Nothing in this report is a project a buyer can book. A buyer who can take an HDB flat or a condo now is not helped by pausing for a model that is still a study.

The demand signal is rental, not a fall in sale prices. A co-living pilot drew more than 600 Singaporeans aged 21 to 35 for just over 100 units at about 30% below market. OCBC’s Chez Anbu put a sustainable rent for young people who still plan to buy at about $1,200 to $1,800 a month. That is a different conversation from an about-$2,000 build-to-rent idea discussed elsewhere. Landlords of today’s flats are not yet competing with a new purpose-built block. The likely tenant, if it is built, is a younger person in a studio or one-bedroom of about 350 to 550 square feet.

Two government land-sale sites for long-stay serviced apartments have been awarded since December 2023, and 21 private-land applications have been approved. That is rental supply at the margin. It does not point HDB or condo prices down. The direction of the ownership market is unchanged: most Singaporeans still prefer to own, and this is a stopgap beside that.
questions: The rental idea is still being explored. Where will you live while you wait for it to be bookable?
A renter who wants their own door is looking now. Is that you, or are you still reading?
What lease that you can sign this month are you leaving unsigned?
n3abc175b.description: The Ministry of National Development said home ownership remains central, and there is also demand for longer-stay rental housing from younger Singaporeans.
n3abc175b.keywords: Singapore property, rent, HDB, condo, new launch, resale, buyers, sellers, market update

zh.title: 新加坡 explores build-to-租金 model demand independent living grows
summary: Borneo Bulletin报道了这则新加坡房地产标题：新加坡 explores build-to-租金 model demand independent living grows。下面的说明是写给买家和卖家的，不是原文照搬。
买房的人要把标题里的数字，拿来和实际的房子、地段、剩余屋契和每月供款比较。先问清楚数字指的是地价、成交价、开价，还是整个市场的变动。
卖房的人不要把一条标题直接套到自己的单位上。准备出售或从组屋升级时，把数字当成要去核实的问题，再对照官方数据或真实挂牌。
facts: 本页来源：Borneo Bulletin
标题：新加坡 explores build-to-租金 model demand independent living grows
takeaways: 等一套建造供出租的房子来代替购买，是在等一个没有日期的东西。国家发展部仍把拥屋放在中心。建造供出租、共居和长住服务式公寓，是在研究给那些想先有自己的地方、或来工作读书的人。这份报道里没有一个可以预订的项目。现在买得起组屋或公寓的人，停下来等一个仍在研究的模式，得不到帮助。
需求信号在租金，不在售价下跌。一项共居试验有超过600名21至35岁的新加坡人，争100多个单位，价钱大约比市价低30%。华侨银行旗下Chez Anbu认为，仍打算以后买房的年轻人，负担得起的租金大约每月1200至1800新元。这和别处讨论的大约2000新元建造供出租，不是同一件事。今天的房东还没有对上新建的专用出租楼。如果建成，租户多半是住约350至550平方英尺单房或一房的年轻人。
2023年12月以来，两幅长住服务式公寓的政府售地已经批出，私人土地上也批准了21份申请。这是边缘上的出租供应。它没有把组屋或公寓售价往下指。拥屋市场的方向没变：多数新加坡人仍想拥有，这只是旁边的一个过渡。
questions: 这个租赁设想还在研究。等它能预订之前，你住在哪里？
想要一扇自己的门的人，现在就在找。那是你，还是你还在读？
这个月你能签的那份租约，为什么还没签？
keypoints: 国家发展部说，拥屋仍然是住房政策的核心。同时，想先独立生活或先租后买的年轻新加坡人，以及来工作或求学的人，也需要可以住得较久的租赁住房。
国家发展部长徐芳达在8月说，当局正在研究建造供出租（build-to-rent）、共享居住和长住型服务式公寓，来回应这种需求。
建造供出租是指整栋房子建来出租多年，而不是在开盘时卖掉。
社会学者陈恩赐说，多数新加坡人还是更想买房。建造供出租可以给想有自己空间的人一个过渡。
新加坡青年计划下的一个共享居住试点，100多个单位吸引了超过600名21岁至35岁的新加坡人。租金大约比市价低30%。
2023年推出的私人长住型服务式公寓，是建造供出租的一种。2023年12月以来，两幅允许这类项目的政府售地已批出，私人土地上有21份申请获批。
华侨银行的Chez Anbu估计，还打算以后买房的年轻人，负担得起的月租大约是1200至1800新元。
一名研究者设想，这类房子大多是约350至550平方英尺的工作室和一房单位，再加上一些两房单位。

The Ministry of National Development said home ownership remains central, and there is also demand for longer-stay rental housing from younger Singaporeans who want to live on their own or rent before they buy, and from people who come to work or study.
National Development Minister Chee Hong Tat said in August that the authorities are looking at build-to-rent, co-living and long-stay serviced apartments for that demand.
Build-to-rent means a block is built to be rented for years, rather than sold off at a launch.
Sociologist Tan Ern Ser said most Singaporeans still prefer to own, and a build-to-rent option could be a stopgap for people who want their own space.
A co-living pilot under the SG Youth Plan drew interest from more than 600 Singaporeans aged 21 to 35 for just over 100 units, priced about 30% below market.

Private long-stay serviced apartments, introduced in 2023, are one form of build-to-rent. Since December 2023, two government land-sale sites for them have been awarded, and 21 applications on private land have been approved.
OCBC’s Chez Anbu put a sustainable rent for young people who still plan to buy later at about $1,200 to $1,800 a month.
One researcher pictured mostly studios and one-bedroom units of about 350 to 550 square feet, plus some two-bedroom units.

summary: SavePoint Gaming carried this Singapore property headline: IKEA Singapore and City Energy Partner on Smarter Home Design for BTO and HDB Owners. The notes below are for buyers and sellers. They are not a copy of the original article.

HDB buyers should compare the headline with the actual flat, the remaining lease, the town and the monthly mortgage. Ask what the number refers to: a land bid, a transacted resale price, an asking price, or a whole-market move.

HDB sellers should not copy one headline price onto their own block. Buyers will ask about floor, lease and condition. If you are timing a sale or an HDB upgrade, use the figure as a question to research, then confirm it on the official data or the listing itself.
facts: Source named on this page: SavePoint Gaming
Headline: IKEA Singapore and City Energy Partner on Smarter Home Design for BTO and HDB Owners
takeaways: No. The partnership does not move a ballot or a resale price. It is a fit-out service at IKEA Alexandra and IKEA Tampines, announced on 3 November 2026, for someone who already has a home to renovate. Waiting to buy because gas appliances can now be planned with an IKEA kitchen delays the purchase and does not improve the price. An owner who already has keys can use it when they are ready. The service has helped 300 homeowners since a 2025 soft launch. That is a renovation count, not a housing count.

The person who gains is a BTO or resale owner redoing a kitchen: one IKEA contact, then City Energy for hob, hood, water heater, dryer, piping and activation. A tenant does not get this unless the landlord is paying for the works. A seller of an older flat may be asked whether town gas and a gas heater are already there. City Energy’s 2026 figure is that about half of HDB homes on town gas also use a gas water heater, and town gas is in every new HDB flat. That is a feature, not a valuation.

There is no price signal for HDB or condos. The practical effect is less friction for kitchens in new and existing flats, including internet-connected gas appliances. The resale index does not move because a furniture shop added a gas partner.
questions: The flat you are fitting out already has a date. What are you still postponing inside it?
Owners who are renovating now will finish first. Where is your flat in that queue?
A design partner does not choose your home. Which flat are you committing to?

facts: 本页来源：SavePoint Gaming
标题：IKEA 新加坡 City Energy Partner Smarter 住宅 Design 预购组屋组屋 Owners
takeaways: 不会。合作不影响抽签，也不改转售价。它是2026年11月3日宣布的装修服务，在宜家亚历山大和宜家淡滨尼，给已经有房子要装修的人。因为煤气电器现在可以和宜家的厨房一起规划，就推迟买房，只会耽误购买，不会让价钱更好。已经拿到钥匙的人，准备好再用。这项服务自2025年试办以来帮过300个屋主。那是装修的数字，不是房屋供应的数字。
得益的是在重做厨房的预购组屋或转售屋主：宜家一个联络人，然后由城市能源处理炉具、抽油烟机、热水器、干衣机、煤气管和开通。租户得不到，除非房东出钱做工程。旧组屋的卖家可能会被问到已有没有城市煤气和煤气热水器。城市能源2026年的数字是，使用城市煤气的组屋家庭大约一半也用煤气热水器，而所有新组屋都有城市煤气。这是一个条件，不是估价。
组屋和公寓都没有价格信号。实际影响是新房子和现有房子做厨房更省事，包括可联网的煤气电器。家具店多了一个煤气伙伴，转售指数不会因此动。
questions: 你在装修的那套组屋已经有工期。屋子里你还在推迟什么？
现在就开工的屋主会先做完。你的房子排在哪里？
一个设计伙伴不会替你选房子。你要定下来的是哪一套？
keypoints: 新加坡宜家把城市能源旗下的家居方案品牌Life by City Energy，加进了它的家居设计服务。
合作在2026年11月3日宣布，可在宜家亚历山大和宜家淡滨尼使用。
这是这项一站式服务加入的第一个伙伴。服务从2025年试运行以来，已经协助300个家庭。
装修新的预购组屋、翻新房子或重做厨房的人，可以把煤气炉、抽油烟机、煤气热水器和煤气干衣机，和宜家的布局、橱柜、收纳和灯具一起规划。
宜家的设计专员仍然是唯一联系人。如果选了煤气电器，会在动工前请城市能源处理电器尺寸、摆放和煤气管道，之后再协调送货、橱柜、煤气工程和开通。
城市能源说，所有新组屋都有城市煤气。它2026年的数据显示，使用城市煤气的组屋家庭里，大约一半也使用煤气热水器。
产品包括可联网的煤气电器，目的是更省电、也让住户更方便控制。
IKEA Singapore has added Life by City Energy, the home-solutions arm of the town-gas provider, to its Home Design Service.
The partnership was announced on 3 November 2026 and is available at IKEA Alexandra and IKEA Tampines.
It is the first partner added to the end-to-end service, which has helped 300 homeowners since a soft launch in 2025.
Someone furnishing a new BTO flat, renovating, or redoing a kitchen can plan gas hobs, cooker hoods, gas water heaters and gas dryers together with IKEA’s layouts, cabinets, storage and lighting.

The IKEA specialist stays the single contact. If gas appliances are chosen, City Energy is brought in for appliance size, placement and gas piping before work starts, then for delivery, cabinets, gas works and activation.
City Energy says town gas is available in all new HDB flats. Its 2026 data says about half of HDB homes that use town gas also use a gas water heater.
The range includes internet-connected gas appliances, aimed at using less energy and giving the household more control.

summary: DollarsAndSense.sg carried this Singapore property headline: At What Point Does Lease Decay Start Affecting The Value Of Your HDB Flat?. The notes below are for buyers and sellers. They are not a copy of the original article.

HDB buyers should compare the headline with the actual flat, the remaining lease, the town and the monthly mortgage. Ask what the number refers to: a land bid, a transacted resale price, an asking price, or a whole-market move.

HDB sellers should not copy one headline price onto their own block. Buyers will ask about floor, lease and condition. If you are timing a sale or an HDB upgrade, use the figure as a question to research, then confirm it on the official data or the listing itself.
facts: Source named on this page: DollarsAndSense.sg
Headline: At What Point Does Lease Decay Start Affecting The Value Of Your HDB Flat?
takeaways: Waiting while a lease runs down usually costs value. It does not create a bargain in the way a wave of new flats might. The Leasehold Table adopted in 2000 falls slowly for about the first 60 years and more steeply in the last 30. A buyer of an older flat should test the remaining lease against the youngest buyer’s age to 95 before talking about price. If the lease fails that test, the full loan and the full CPF grant are already off the table, whether the headline price looks soft or not.

Sellers who count on a future buyer paying up in hope of SERS are who Lawrence Wong warned about in 2017, when he said prices come down as leases run down, especially near the end. For some owners at 65, Lease Buyback is the exit: keep at least 30 years, sell the tail to HDB, and top up CPF, with a bonus of up to $30,000. In the worked example, a fully paid four-room valued at $450,000 with 65 years left had a 35-year tail priced at $190,000. That is retirement cash, not a resale comparable a young buyer can use. About 16,000 households have used the scheme since 2009.

The direction is a slow drag that steepens late, not a 2026 shock. As of 2025, 77.2% of resident households live in HDB flats, so this is the mass market’s long-run constraint. Future buyers who need financing will keep choosing leases long enough to last. Short leases clear only for buyers who can live with cash and a shorter horizon.
questions: The lease on the flat you want is already counting down. What year are you waiting to check it?
A buyer who needs the lease to reach 95 is shopping now. Are they looking at your flat?
What does another year of delay do to the lease you could have bought this month?

zh.title: What Point Does Lease Decay Start Affecting Value 组屋组屋?
summary: DollarsAndSense.sg报道了这则新加坡房地产标题：What Point Does Lease Decay Start Affecting Value 组屋组屋?。下面的说明是写给买家和卖家的，不是原文照搬。
买房的人要把标题里的数字，拿来和实际的房子、地段、剩余屋契和每月供款比较。先问清楚数字指的是地价、成交价、开价，还是整个市场的变动。
卖房的人不要把一条标题直接套到自己的单位上。准备出售或从组屋升级时，把数字当成要去核实的问题，再对照官方数据或真实挂牌。
facts: 本页来源：DollarsAndSense.sg
标题：What Point Does Lease Decay Start Affecting Value 组屋组屋?
takeaways: 一边等、一边让屋契变短，通常是在损耗价值。它不会像一批新组屋那样制造便宜。2000年采用的地契表，大约前60年跌得慢，最后30年跌得更陡。买旧组屋的人，谈价钱之前先用剩余屋契对照最年轻买家到95岁。过不了这一关，全额贷款和全额公积金补助已经没有了，跟标题看起来便不便宜无关。
指望未来买家为了选择性整体重建而付高价的卖家，就是黄循财2017年提醒的人。他当时说，屋契尤其到了尾段，价钱会下降。对部分65岁的业主，屋契回购是出路：自己至少留下30年，把尾段卖给建屋局，补进公积金，奖金最高3万新元。例子里，一套已付清、估价45万、还剩65年的四房，35年的尾段定价19万。那是退休现金，不是年轻买家用得了的转售可比价。2009年以来大约1万6000个家庭用过这个计划。
方向是缓慢的拖累，到后期变陡，不是2026年的冲击。截至2025年，77.2%的居民家庭住在组屋，所以这是大众市场的长期约束。需要贷款的未来买家，会继续选够长的屋契。短屋契只有付得起现金、也接受较短年期的人会接手。
questions: 你想要的那套组屋，屋契已经在倒数。你还要等到哪一年才去查？
需要屋契覆盖到95岁的买家现在就在找。他们看的是你的房子吗？
这个月能买下的屋契，再拖一年会变成什么？
keypoints: 文章解释的是屋契减值：组屋是99年地契，剩余年限越短，价值越低。截至2025年，77.2%的居民家庭住在组屋。
2017年黄循财还是国家发展部长时说，屋契尤其到了尾段，房价会跟着下降。他当时担心有人把旧组屋卖出高价，指望选择性整体重建计划（SERS）。
2009年推出的屋契回购计划，让屋主把一部分剩余屋契卖给建屋局，继续住在屋里，并把所得补进公积金退休户头。建屋局可能再给最多3万新元的红利。
2009年以来，大约1万6000个家庭用过这个计划。
2019年到2023年，平均所得加红利大约是：五房或更大261000新元，四房212000新元，三房168000新元，两房153000新元，一房98000新元。
建屋局的例子是一套已还清、估值45万新元、还剩65年屋契的四房。65岁的屋主至少保留30年，可以把尾段的35年卖出。例子里这35年值19万新元，比他们留下的30年更不值钱，尽管尾段更长。
新加坡土地局在2000年7月31日采用租契表，也叫Bala’s Table。它把有年限的地契定成永久地契价值的一个百分比。曲线在大约前60年下降较慢，最后30年下降更快。
新加坡管理大学2025年的一篇论文说，有充分证据显示，建屋局在为两房灵活单位定价，以及为屋契回购计划估价时，用了这张表。
The article explains lease decay: an HDB flat is on a 99-year lease, and its value falls as that lease runs down. As of 2025, 77.2% of resident households live in HDB flats.

In 2017, when he was National Development Minister, Lawrence Wong said prices come down as leases run down, especially near the end. He was worried about older flats being sold at high prices in the hope of SERS.
The Lease Buyback Scheme, started in 2009, lets an owner sell part of the remaining lease to HDB, keep living in the flat, and top up a CPF Retirement Account. HDB may add a bonus of up to $30,000.
About 16,000 households have used the scheme since 2009.
From 2019 to 2023, the average proceeds plus bonus were about $261,000 for a 5-room or larger flat, $212,000 for a 4-room, $168,000 for a 3-room, $153,000 for a 2-room and $98,000 for a 1-room.

HDB’s worked example is a fully paid 4-room flat valued at $450,000 with 65 years left. Owners aged 65 keep at least 30 years and can sell the remaining 35 years. That tail is priced at $190,000 in the example, less than the 30 years they keep, even though the tail is longer.

The Singapore Land Authority adopted the Leasehold Table, also called Bala’s Table, on 31 July 2000. It prices a leasehold as a percentage of freehold value. The curve falls slowly for about the first 60 years, then more steeply in the last 30.
A 2025 Singapore Management University paper said there was compelling evidence that HDB used Bala’s Table when pricing 2-room Flexi flats and when valuing leases for the Lease Buyback Scheme.

summary: FZINE Singapore carried this Singapore property headline: Get Your S*** Together: When Is The Right Time To Apply For A BTO With My Partner?. The notes below are for buyers and sellers. They are not a copy of the original article.

HDB buyers should compare the headline with the actual flat, the remaining lease, the town and the monthly mortgage. Ask what the number refers to: a land bid, a transacted resale price, an asking price, or a whole-market move.

HDB sellers should not copy one headline price onto their own block. Buyers will ask about floor, lease and condition. If you are timing a sale or an HDB upgrade, use the figure as a question to research, then confirm it on the official data or the listing itself.
facts: Source named on this page: FZINE Singapore
Headline: Get Your S*** Together: When Is The Right Time To Apply For A BTO With My Partner?
takeaways: The article’s own range is about two years together, from Timothy, to four years in Clara and Tim’s case, and Clara’s point is that there is no fixed number. Applying early, as Theresa puts it, is practical only because the wait for a flat is long, and only if the couple already shares a commitment. Waiting for that commitment reduces the chance of a breakup during a multi-year queue. Applying before it exists risks a joint flat that is hard to unwind. The impact of waiting is a later ballot, against whatever supply is on sale then. It does not make the construction wait shorter.

This is not a seller’s pricing story. Couples who decide they will not wait become resale buyers. Couples who ballot are out of the resale market for the length of the queue and then the occupation period. A seller of a resale flat meets the first group, not the second.
There is no price call. The timing that matters is the couple’s, set against a long public queue. A later application does not buy a cheaper market. It buys a different exercise.
questions: The couples in the piece have already applied or already decided. Where is your application?
The wait for a flat is long either way. What does another year of not applying change?
If you are not balloting, which resale flat are the two of you going to see?

facts: 本页来源：FZINE Singapore
标题：Get S*** Together: When Right Time Apply 预购组屋 My Partner?
takeaways: 文章自己的范围，是Timothy说的至少大约两年，到Clara和Tim的四年。Clara的重点是没有固定年数。像Theresa说的，早点申请之所以实际，是因为等组屋的时间很长，而且只有在两人已经有共同承诺时才成立。等到那个承诺，可以降低在多年轮候里分手的可能。承诺还没有就申请，风险是一套很难拆开的联名组屋。等待的影响是更晚才抽签，面对的是当时在卖的供应。它不会把建造的等候缩短。
这不是卖家的定价故事。决定不等的伴侣，会变成转售买家。去抽签的伴侣，在轮候和之后的居住年限里离开转售市场。转售组屋的卖家遇到的是前一种人，不是后一种。
这里没有价格判断。要紧的时间是这对伴侣的，对照的是公共组屋很长的轮候。晚一点申请，买不到一个更便宜的市场。买到的是另一轮销售。
questions: 文中的伴侣已经申请，或者已经做了决定。你的申请在哪里？
等一套组屋，怎么等都久。再一年不申请，会改变什么？
如果你们不抽签，两个人要去看哪一套转售组屋？
keypoints: 这篇文章问的是，一对伴侣什么时候应该一起申请预购组屋（BTO）。谈的是时机，不是一次新的开卖。
Clara说没有固定的年数。她和Tim在一起四年后才申请。
Timothy的看法是，一对伴侣至少在一起大约两年。
Theresa说，因为等组屋的时间很长，早点申请可以比较实际，但只有在两个人已经有共同承诺的时候。
Clara、Tim、Timothy和Theresa说的是个人看法。这篇文章不是建屋局的规定，也不是一次开卖。
The article asks when a couple should apply together for a Build-To-Order flat. It is about timing, not a new launch.
Clara says there is no fixed number of years. She and Tim applied after four years together.
Timothy’s view is that a couple should have been together for at least about two years.
Theresa says applying early can be practical because the wait for a flat is long, and only when the couple already shares a commitment.
Clara, Tim, Timothy and Theresa are giving personal views. The piece is not an HDB rule and not a sales launch.

facts: Source named on this page: EdgeProp.sg
Headline: UOB prices 38 Marina Collection units from $1,269 psf, below recent Sentosa Cove resales
Figure in the headline: $1,269 psf
takeaways: UOB is a motivated seller of 38 units at Marina Collection, from $1,269 per square foot, with an average ask around $1,340 per square foot, about 20% below this year’s Sentosa Cove resale average. Waiting for a second batch this explicit is a bet, not a fact in the report. Twelve units are vacant and 26 are tenanted on leases running from the fourth quarter of 2026 to the fourth quarter of 2028. A buyer who needs to live there must take a vacant unit or wait out a lease. That wait is a tenancy, not a better price.

The buyer who can use the list can write from about $2.588 million for a three-bedroom up to about $3.11 million for a four-bedroom, in a 124-unit project launched in late 2007 and completed in 2011. Zaobao’s lowest per-square-foot ask is a ground-floor four-bedroom with a private enclosed space, 2,390 square feet, at about $3.03 million. Another Cove seller who matches that is matching a bank sale tied to an old inflated-loan case, not an owner who can hold. PropNex is the exclusive agent, so the ask is organised, not a scatter of distressed owners.

The direction is a clearance inside one Cove project, in line with the wider point that Sentosa Cove is harder to sell than freehold city stock. It is not a decline in mainland condos. Buyers who can choose the mainland can ignore the list. Buyers who want the Cove have a current asking range to test against.

summary: The Independent Singapore carried this Singapore property headline: 5-room HDB flat with 94 years left on lease sold for S$1.8 billion; highest resale price ever in Singapore. The headline gives these figures: S$1.8. The notes below are for buyers and sellers. They are not a copy of the original article.

HDB buyers should compare the headline with the actual flat, the remaining lease, the town and the monthly mortgage. Ask what the number refers to: a land bid, a transacted resale price, an asking price, or a whole-market move.

HDB sellers should not copy one headline price onto their own block. Buyers will ask about floor, lease and condition. If you are timing a sale or an HDB upgrade, use the figure as a question to research, then confirm it on the official data or the listing itself.
facts: Source named on this page: The Independent Singapore
Headline: 5-room HDB flat with 94 years left on lease sold for S$1.8 billion; highest resale price ever in Singapore
Figure in the headline: S$1.8
takeaways: The figure to use is S$1.818 million, not S$1.8 billion. Acting on the billion number would be acting on a mistake. Even the million-dollar print is one five-room flat at Block 96 Dawson Road, SkyParc @ Dawson, about 1,195 square feet on storeys 40 to 42, with about 94 years left. Waiting for this sale to pull ordinary five-room prices up or down is waiting on the wrong flat. From June 2025 to September 2026, one five-room on Holland Drive and four on Dawson Road sold between $1.58 million and $1.7 million.

The seller who can use the print owns one of the 74 five-room flats in that 284-unit block. The buyer who paid it beat more than eight offers, and the top three were above $1.8 million. That buyer wanted size, a central address, amenities and a view, in a project completed in 2020. A seller of a smaller Queenstown flat, or of a five-room somewhere else, does not have this buyer.

The top of central HDB resale is still being bid, including a $1.7 million sale in the same project in February. That is the direction of a scarce product: new, large, high floor, long lease, Queenstown. It is not the direction of the HDB index, and it is not a billion-dollar market.
questions: The figure in the report is one flat. Is the flat you are pricing that flat?
Buyers will ask which home they are actually buying. When do you show them yours?
What are you waiting to correct before you offer on the Dawson flat that is for sale now?

summary: Real Estate Asia carried this Singapore property headline: Singapore's higher income ceiling may intensify November BTO competition. The notes below are for buyers and sellers. They are not a copy of the original article.

HDB buyers should compare the headline with the actual flat, the remaining lease, the town and the monthly mortgage. Ask what the number refers to: a land bid, a transacted resale price, an asking price, or a whole-market move.

HDB sellers should not copy one headline price onto their own block. Buyers will ask about floor, lease and condition. If you are timing a sale or an HDB upgrade, use the figure as a question to research, then confirm it on the official data or the listing itself.
facts: Source named on this page: Real Estate Asia
Headline: Singapore's higher income ceiling may intensify November BTO competition
takeaways: This report was written on 22 October, before the November launch. From August 2026 the ceiling is $16,000 a month for couples and families and $8,000 for singles. A wider ceiling means more households in the same exercise. The report said that weighs most on applicants without a priority ballot. For that buyer, waiting did not thin the crowd. It left them in a larger one. Missing the exercise then means waiting for a later sale with no promise of easier odds.

The new competitors are middle-income families and higher-earning couples without children. A household at $16,000 a month was described as able to borrow up to about $909,372 and buy a flat up to about $1.212 million, so they can reach flats that used to sit outside their limit. Resale sellers in that band may meet people who could also have balloted. They are not losing the buyer who needs keys now. The future BTO buyer accepts the wait. The resale buyer will not.

The direction expected then was a more competitive November, with nearly 8,000 flats. More eligible buyers against one exercise is tighter odds for people without priority. On this report it is not a rise in resale prices. It is a change in who can join the ballot.
questions: Did the higher income ceiling make waiting a worse idea for November?
